title: Measles deaths reach 1,289 as suspected cases pass 240,000
excerpt: Five more children died in the 24 hours to 8am on 10 November. More than 215,000 suspected patients have been admitted to hospital since 15 March.
content:
Five more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours to 8am on Tuesday, 10 November, bringing deaths this year to 1,289, according to Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) data reported by The Business Standard.

The numbers

  • Deaths: 1,289, of which 1,184 were suspected measles and 105 laboratory-confirmed.
  • Suspected cases: 241,556, including 1,357 in the latest 24 hours.
  • Confirmed cases: 24,610, including 87 in the latest 24 hours.
  • Hospital admissions: 215,540 suspected patients since 15 March, of whom 206,799 have recovered.

Devlens reported 1,282 deaths on 8 November, so seven more deaths have been recorded in two days. New suspected cases are still above 1,000 a day.

Why it matters

The outbreak is running alongside a heavy dengue season, with more than 6,000 dengue patients in hospital on 10 November, so district and children’s hospitals face both at once. Health and nutrition NGOs can help find children who missed routine vaccination and refer sick children early, particularly malnourished children, who face a higher risk of dying from measles.

What to watch

Whether daily suspected cases fall below 1,000, and any announcement of a further catch-up vaccination round.

Sources
